title: THE ODDS RECEIPT
goal: Revise a scary probability using real reference points and opposing evidence.

title: THE NEW-INFORMATION TEST
goal: Test whether more analysis is adding information before giving it another round.

steps.text: Notice whether this round of analysis has produced any genuinely new information.
Separate what happened from the role you are assigning yourself.
Set any extra work aside.
Check the first action against one immediate fact.
Reduce the remaining question to three words.

win: No-new-information analysis was stopped and the remaining question was reduced to a small, usable form.
mindBend: Thinking harder cannot extract new evidence from a closed information set. The moment analysis stops producing novelty is a legitimate stopping signal.

title: PROOF THROUGH ONE WINDOW
goal: Stop demanding final proof when the existing evidence is already enough to choose the next action.

steps.text: State a single direct reality about the situation.
Pinpoint the final proof your mind is demanding.
Ask whether that proof would change the decision or only change the feeling of certainty.
Choose the next action using the evidence you already have.
Stop the review after that one decision.

win: The last proof demand was tested for usefulness and the review ended after one evidence-based decision.
mindBend: If extra proof would change only the feeling of certainty, not the decision, it is no longer decision information.
